messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: KV cache prefix count spike in us-east-1 detected by metric kv.cache.prefix_count > 1M for 3m, eviction_rate spiking, and continuous-batcher latency climb. autoscaler activity detected: rapid scale-ups then scale-downs in last 12m. Dash: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/kvcache/kv-cache-overview (pagerduty: P12345)

maria: acked. paging @pagerduty-oncall. tagging SRE + eng-runtime. I'm taking initial triage. anyone oncall for runtime? :alarm_clock:

trent: i'm oncall, jumping in. seeing p50 token generation latency up ~2.1s -> 4.8s, p95 up to 11s. KV cache unique prefixes jumped 12x around 02:06 UTC. correlates with a config push at 02:03 that toggled continuous_batching.experimental_prefix_merge=true (deploy: d5a3f2c).

kai: I merged that change as part of batching perf tests. The prefix merge was meant to reduce duplicate batches but it looks like it's creating many small cache keys instead. initial guess: prefix normalization bug -> combinatorial prefix explosion per request pattern.

aj: autoscaler notes: HPA saw CPU surge then fell; minReplicas=1, maxReplicas=20, CPU target 60%. Because cache miss cost is high, pods spin up, warmup finishes, then batching/kvcache warms and CPU drops, causing scale down -> repeat thrash. we should stop the oscillation by stabilizing HPA or bumping minReplicas temporarily.

elaine: customer impact: Support queue has 3 priority customers reporting elevated 5xx for LLM endpoints since ~02:10. Sample error from logs: "error=kv_lookup_timeout prefix=\"user:ctx:ab12...\"". attaching snippet: https://logs.redwood.internal/stream/abcd1234

trent: quick mitigation plan: 1) flip experimental_prefix_merge=false via runtime feature flag (fast) 2) increase HPA minReplicas to 4 and set stabilizationWindowSeconds to 180s 3) temporarily reduce batching window to 10ms for affected pool to avoid small-batch overload. executing now.

maria: do it. I'll coordinate customer comms and handoff. @kai please confirm the flag path.

kai: flag is in config service under /runtime/batching/experimental_prefix_merge. patching with rollouts API. command:

```bash
# flip feature flag
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -d '{"path":"/runtime/batching/experimental_prefix_merge","value":false}' \
  https://config.redwood.internal/v1/flags/patch

# bump HPA minReplicas
kubectl -n inference patch hpa inference-runtime-hpa -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":4}}'

# set stabilization window
kubectl -n inference patch hpa inference-runtime-hpa -p '{"spec":{"behavior":{"scaleDown":{"stabilizationWindowSeconds":180}}}}'
```

trent: applied flag flip at 02:18 UTC (rollout id r-984a). patched HPA minReplicas -> 4 at 02:19. reduced batch window for pool 'us-east-1-prod' from 25ms -> 10ms at 02:21 via:

```yaml
# partial config applied
pool: us-east-1-prod
batching:
  window_ms: 10
  max_tokens: 1024
```

maria: good. I'll message 3 impacted customers with a short heads-up and ETA for full postmortem. Draft: "We're investigating elevated 5xx and latency; a runtime config change is being rolled back; we expect service to stabilize within 30m. We'll follow up with a timeline and root cause." ok? :thumbsup:

elaine: looks good. include that we have a temporary mitigation in place.

trent: monitoring: after changes, prefix_count down ~78% within 6m, eviction_rate back to normal, p95 down from 11s -> 3.1s, error rate dropping. still watching for residual thrash.

kai: confirmed no regressions in canary. preliminary root cause: prefix_merge created unique keys per dynamic signal (e.g., user session ids leak into prefix normalization). needs code revert and unit test coverage to prevent combinatorial prefixes.

aj: follow-ups for autoscale: propose adding cooldowns and use a composite metric (predicted_qps + CPU) rather than raw CPU to avoid reactive spin-ups. also add pod readiness probe to delay HPA reaction until kv cache warmup completes. filing ticket.

trent: creating incident ticket now: INC-2026-358 with timeline, actions, and owner. assigning to eng-runtime + eng-ml for RCA.

maria: handing over to night oncall @pagerduty-oncall at 03:05 UTC. please escalate back to this thread if anything flares. I'll update status page with short note.

pagerduty-oncall: acknowledged. continuing watch.

kai: postmortem TODOs: revert commit d5a3f2c, add deterministic prefix hashing + unit test, add perf test that simulates high-cardinality prefixes, and add rollout guard (fail if prefix_count increases > 3x in canary window).

trent: low-priority follow-up: add a dashboard alert for prefix_count delta to trigger before autoscaler. also add a circuit breaker to batching to disable merging if prefix cardinality > threshold.

maria: Great work team. closing active paging. I'll file a customer-facing postmortem draft and link here once ready. next steps assigned to tickets. :white_check_mark: 

kai: metrics now look stable for 18m, tail latency within SLOs. closing loop.

elaine: adding affected customers + internal dashboards to postmortem.

trent: note for playbook update: when batch-related CPU thrash + cache cardinality spike happen together -> immediate steps: flip batching flag, bump HPA min replicas, apply stabilization window, reduce batch window. Save as playbook entry.

maria: handoff complete. tagging follow-ups: ENG-RT-642 (revert + tests), SRE-354 (autoscaler tuning), DEVEX-128 (playbook update). thanks everyone. :pray:
